---
title: "Markdown Input Schema"
page-layout: article
---

This page is the reference for writing questions in Markdown: the YAML front matter and the
body syntax. One question per file; the body becomes the question text, in Markdown unless
`format` says otherwise. Read a file with `questionsafe render`/`validate` on the command line
or `Reader(path).read()` in Python.

## Common fields (all types)

- type: string
  - One of: singlechoice (aliases `single`, `sc`), multichoice (`multiple`, `multi`, `mc`),
    truefalse (`tf`), shortanswer (`short`, `sa`), numerical (`num`), essay, description
    (`desc`), cloze, metachoice (a template, not a single question; read with
    `Reader.read_metachoice()`)
- name: string
- defaultgrade: float
- tags: list[str]
- id: string
- questiontext_format or format: string (default: markdown). Plain-string choices
  (singlechoice, multichoice, MetaChoice), stems, feedback, hints, and essay grader info
  inherit this format; `{text, format}` sets it per text. Moodle reads it the same way: an
  answer or feedback without its own format takes the question text's. Not inherited: short
  answer, numerical, and truefalse answers (Moodle stores them as plain text), and the essay
  response template (see Essay).
- feedback.general: string or {text, format}

### Hints and penalty (where supported)

- hints: list of string or {text, format}
- hint_penalty: float

### Combined feedback (where supported)

- feedback.correct: string or {text, format}
- feedback.partiallycorrect: string or {text, format}
- feedback.incorrect: string or {text, format}

Notes:
- When a question type does not support a configuration (e.g., combined feedback for SingleChoice), the importer will emit a warning and ignore it.
- If conflicting configurations are given (e.g., both answers and choices), the importer raises an error.

### Shared front matter: include

`include:` merges front matter from other files: one path or a list of paths, each a YAML
file or a Markdown file whose front matter is used.

```yaml
---
include: [course-defaults.yml, ../shared/feedback.md]
type: singlechoice
name: Japan/Capital
---
```

- Keys in the file itself win over included keys; among includes, the first file wins.
  `Reader(path).read(include_warn=True)` warns about each overridden key.
- Relative paths resolve against the question file's directory (or `Reader(answer_dir=...)`).
- Includes are single-level: an `include:` inside an included file is ignored.

The front matter may also wrap the question keys in `question:`; keys inside it win over
top-level keys.

### Paths and variables

`include:`, cloze `file:`, and essay `{path: ...}` values expand `~`, `$VAR`, and `${VAR}`.
Variables come from `variables:` in `questionsafe.yml` in the current directory, then from
the environment:

```yaml
# questionsafe.yml
variables:
  ROOT: /path/to/shared
```

Image paths expand `~` but not variables; they resolve against the question file's
directory (see Images).

## Choices in the body

For singlechoice, multichoice, and truefalse, choices can be written as a checkbox list
under the reserved heading `/choices` instead of front matter `choices:`:

```markdown
---
type: singlechoice
name: AS
---

Which statement about the AS curve is correct?

## /choices

- (x) The AS curve slopes upward
  because some prices are sticky.
- ( ) The AS curve is vertical when all prices are sticky.
```

- `(x)` or `(o)` (either case) marks a correct choice, `( )` a wrong one,
  as in front matter `choices:`. Indented lines continue the choice above.
- Text before the first reserved heading is the question text.
- A reserved heading is a heading of any level whose text starts with `/`.
  Reserved names: `/choices`. An unknown name is an error; so is giving
  both front matter `choices:` and `/choices`.
- To keep such a heading as question text, end it with `{.noqs}`
  (`## /choices {.noqs}`); the marker is removed. Headings inside code fences are never reserved.

## Math

Write TeX with `\( ... \)` (inline) and `\[ ... \]` (display), as in any Markdown text:

```markdown
Let \( Y = C + I \) and \( \{x : x > 0\} \).
```

Texts with `format: markdown` stay Markdown in Moodle; when writing the XML, questionsafe
backslash-escapes the Markdown specials inside each math span, so Moodle's Markdown
converter hands the TeX to MathJax unchanged (without this, `\(` loses its backslash and
`*`/`_` become emphasis). The original text is unchanged; only the XML carries the escapes,
which is also what you see when editing the question in Moodle. Code spans and fences are
left alone, and `\\(` is a literal `\(`, not math.

`$...$` is not math: Moodle's MathJax filter does not treat `$` as a delimiter by default.
Moodle shows the math only with the MathJax filter enabled (it is by default).

## Images

Question text and choices (singlechoice, multichoice, MetaChoice pools) can show local
images, written as `![alt](path)` or `<img src="path">` (in HTML texts, `<img>` only):

```markdown
Which shift does the figure show? ![The AS curve](img/as-curve.png)

## /choices

- (x) ![left](img/correct-shift-left.png)
- ( ) ![right](img/shift-right.png)
```

- A relative path is relative to the Markdown file. From Python, it is relative to the
  current directory.
- Each image is embedded in the Moodle XML under the first 12 hex digits of its content
  hash (`3f9a1c2b7e4d.png`), so the author's file name never reaches the student.
- In choices, the alt text becomes `Choice image` and the title is dropped: a descriptive
  one would give the answer away. The question text keeps the author's alt text.
- PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP only. SVG is an error: its text is visible in the page source.
  A missing file is an error too.
- URLs (`https://...`) and images inside code are left alone.
- With shuffle on, choices are written in an order fixed by a hash of their text, not in
  the authoring order. Moodle numbers answers in XML order and shows the number in image
  URLs, so a correct choice written first would otherwise be the lowest number.

## Choice layout

singlechoice and multichoice take the layout settings either under `choice_layout:` or as
top-level keys named as in Moodle XML. Giving both names for one setting is an error.

| `choice_layout:` | Moodle XML key | Moodle edit form | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `numbering` | `answernumbering` | Number the choices? | `abc`, `ABCD`, `123`, `iii`, `III`, `none` | `abc` |
| `shuffle` | `shuffleanswers` | Shuffle the choices? | bool | true |
| `single_choice` | `single` | One or multiple answers? | bool | true for singlechoice, false for multichoice |

The defaults are Moodle's. `choice_layout: {labels: ...}` is a deprecated name for `numbering`.
The Python API uses the same names: `set_numbering`, `set_shuffle`, `set_single_choice`,
`set_choice_layout(numbering=..., shuffle=..., single_choice=...)`.

## SingleChoice

Single-answer choice question; exactly one correct answer with fraction=100 and no other positive fractions. Supports choice_layout (numbering/shuffle/single_choice), hints, general feedback, tags, id.

Unsupported: combined feedback (correct/partiallycorrect/incorrect) — ignored with a warning.

### Short-hand

```yaml
---
type: singlechoice
name: str
choices:
  correct: [str]    # exactly one
  wrong: [str, ...]
choice_layout:
  numbering: abc|ABCD|123|iii|III|none  # default abc
  shuffle: bool
tags: [str, ...]
id: str
defaultgrade: float
---
Question stem in Markdown
```

### Full-form

```yaml
---
type: singlechoice
name: str
defaultgrade: float
answers:
  - text: str
    fraction: float                # 100 for the correct; <=0 for wrongs
    feedback: str | {text, format} # optional
answernumbering: abc|ABCD|123|iii|III|none
shuffleanswers: bool
hints:
  - str | {text, format}
hint_penalty: float
feedback:
  general: str | {text, format}
tags: [str, ...]
id: str
---
Question stem in Markdown
```

## MultiChoice

Multiple-choice (checkbox or single radio UI). With checkboxes, positive fractions must sum to 100; with `single_choice: true`, one answer must be 100 and others may give partial credit. Supports choice_layout (numbering/shuffle/single_choice), hints, general and combined feedback.

### Short-hand

```yaml
---
type: multichoice
name: str
choices:
  correct: [str, ...]    # uniformly split to sum 100
  wrong: [str, ...]
choice_layout:
  numbering: abc|ABCD|123|iii|III|none  # default abc
  shuffle: bool
  single_choice: bool  # default false
hints:
  - str | {text, format}
hint_penalty: float
feedback:
  general: str | {text, format}
  correct: str | {text, format}
  partiallycorrect: str | {text, format}
  incorrect: str | {text, format}
tags: [str, ...]
id: str
---
Question stem
```

### Full-form

```yaml
---
type: multichoice
name: str
defaultgrade: float
answers:
  - text: str
    fraction: float                # multiple: positives sum to 100; single: one at 100
    feedback: str | {text, format} # optional
single: bool
answernumbering: abc|ABCD|123|iii|III|none
shuffleanswers: bool
hints:
  - str | {text, format}
hint_penalty: float
feedback:
  general: str | {text, format}
  correct: str | {text, format}
  partiallycorrect: str | {text, format}
  incorrect: str | {text, format}
tags: [str, ...]
id: str
---
Question stem
```

## TrueFalse

Exactly two answers with texts 'true' and 'false'. Supports general feedback only.

### Short-hand

```yaml
---
type: truefalse
name: str
answer: true|false     # also yes/no, t/f, y/n, 1/0
---
Statement to judge
```

The body may also list the two choices under `/choices` (see Choices in the body).

### Full-form

```yaml
---
type: truefalse
name: str
defaultgrade: float
answers:
  - text: true|false
    fraction: 100|0
    feedback: str | {text, format}
feedback:
  general: str | {text, format}
tags: [str, ...]
id: str
---
Question stem
```

## ShortAnswer

Accepted strings with optional fractions. Supports hints/penalty and combined feedback.
One answer must be worth 100%. Moodle grades a response by the first matching answer, so
list specific answers before wildcards such as `*`.

### Short-hand

One accepted answer, at 100%:

```yaml
---
type: shortanswer
name: str
answer: str                        # or {text: str, feedback: str | {text, format}}
case_sensitive: true|false
---
Question stem
```

### Full-form

```yaml
---
type: shortanswer
name: str
defaultgrade: float
answers:
  - text: str
    fraction: float                # default 100
    feedback: str | {text, format} # optional
case_sensitive: true|false         # true: case sensitive (default false)
hints:
  - str | {text, format}
hint_penalty: float
feedback:
  general: str | {text, format}
  correct: str | {text, format}
  partiallycorrect: str | {text, format}
  incorrect: str | {text, format}
tags: [str, ...]
id: str
---
Question stem
```

## Numerical

Numeric answers with optional tolerance. One answer must be worth 100%. Moodle grades a response by the first matching
answer, so list narrower tolerances first.

### Short-hand

One exact answer, at 100%:

```yaml
---
type: numerical
name: str
answer: float                      # a scalar; tolerance and feedback need the full form
---
Question stem
```

### Full-form

```yaml
---
type: numerical
name: str
defaultgrade: float
answers:
  - answer: float
    tolerance: float
    fraction: float                # default 100
    feedback: str | {text, format}
units:                             # optional; the base unit first
  - name: str
    multiplier: float              # default 1
unit_handling: none|optional|graded   # default optional
unit_penalty: float                # 0-1, default 0.1 (graded only)
unit_penalty_of: response|question # default response (graded only)
unit_input: text|radio|select      # default text (graded only)
units_left: true|false             # default false
hints:
  - str | {text, format}
hint_penalty: float
feedback:
  general: str | {text, format}
  correct: str | {text, format}
  partiallycorrect: str | {text, format}
  incorrect: str | {text, format}
tags: [str, ...]
id: str
---
Question stem
```

Values and tolerances are read as decimals and rounded to 15 decimal places, so `0.9` in the
file is the same number as `0.3 + 0.3 + 0.3` in Python.

### Units

Answers are given in the base unit, the first in `units:`. A value in another unit is the
value in the base unit times its `multiplier`: with base `g`, `kg` has multiplier `0.001`.
The defaults are Moodle's.

| Key | Moodle's edit form | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `unit_handling` | Unit handling | `none`: not used; `optional`: a unit, if given, converts the response; `graded`: the unit must be given and is graded |
| `unit_penalty` | Unit penalty | 0-1, deducted for a wrong unit |
| `unit_penalty_of` | (penalty applied) | `response`: as a fraction of the response grade; `question`: of the question grade |
| `unit_input` | Units are input using | `text`: a text box; `radio`: radio buttons; `select`: a drop-down menu |
| `units_left` | Units go | `true`: on the left, as in $1.00 |

In Moodle XML these become `<showunits>` and `<unitgradingtype>`, whose codes depend on each
other; see `UnitSpec.moodle_codes` and [References](references.md).

## Cloze

A cloze question embeds other questions as gaps in its text. Each gap is a separate
Markdown file (singlechoice, multichoice, shortanswer, or numerical); `{{id}}` in the body
marks where it goes.

```yaml
---
type: cloze
name: Japan/Cities
cloze:
  gap1: schoice.md                   # a path
  gap2: {file: mchoice.md, orientation: h, weight: 2}
---

The capital of Japan is {{gap1}}.

Choose stations in Tokyo. {{gap2}}
```

- A gap is a path, or a mapping with `file`, `orientation`, and `weight`. A list of
  one-key mappings (`- file: ...`, `- weight: 2`) is read the same way.
- `orientation`: for singlechoice, omitted = dropdown, `v` = vertical radio buttons,
  `h` = horizontal; for multichoice, omitted or `v` = vertical checkboxes, `h` = horizontal.
- `weight`: the gap's share of the grade, a non-negative integer (default 1).
- Gap files resolve against the cloze file's directory (or `Reader(question_dir=...)`)
  and expand variables (see Paths and variables). A gap file's question text is not used.
- Without `cloze:`, the body is used as is, so it may contain Moodle cloze syntax written
  by hand.

## Essay

Essay/free-text question. No graded answers, but rich response configuration is supported.

```yaml
---
type: essay
name: str
defaultgrade: float
response:
  textarea:
    format: editor|editorfilepicker|monospaced|plain|noinline
    required: bool
    lines: int
    min_words: int
    max_words: int
    template: str | {text, format} | { path: str }
  attachments:
    count: int
    required: bool
    maxbytes: int
    filetypelist: [str, ...]
graderinfo: str | {text, format} | { path: str }
feedback:
  general: str | {text, format}
tags: [str, ...]
id: str
---
Question prompt
```

Notes:
- If textarea.format is "noinline", then attachments.count must be > 0 and attachments.required must be true.
- The response template is the answer box's initial text. Moodle inserts it as-is: its
  `format` is not applied, and math in it is not escaped. Write it for textarea.format:
  HTML for the editor, plain text for plain and monospaced. A plain string has format html.
- When template is given as { path: "..." } or graderinfo is { path: "..." }, the Reader expands ~, $VAR, and ${VAR} using variables from questionsafe.yml in the current working directory (falling back to environment variables).

## Description

Informational text; no answers.

```yaml
---
type: description
name: str
feedback:
  general: str | {text, format}
tags: [str, ...]
id: str
---
Description body
```

## MetaChoice

A `type: metachoice` file describes a variant-generation template, not a single
question: a shared choice pool, several stems, and constraints. `Reader.read()`
rejects it; use `Reader.read_metachoice()`, which returns a `MetaChoice`.
Generation parameters (`n`, `limit`, `seed`, `prototype`) are not part of the
file; they belong to the exam build that calls `generate_multichoice()` or
`generate_singlechoice()`.

````markdown
---
type: metachoice
name: str                       # required; variants are named "{name}/{stem key}"
choices:                        # required: key -> str | {text, format}
  KEY: str | {text, format}
stems:                          # required: key -> str | {text, format}
  STEM: str | {text, format}
constraints:                    # optional: id -> spec
  some_id:
    members: [KEY, ...]         # required, all keys must be in choices
    min: int                    # default 0
    max: int                    # omitted = unbounded
    apply_to: [STEM, ...]       # omitted = global; listed = local to those stems
---
Free commentary (ignored by the Reader).

```csv
choice,STEM_A,STEM_B
KEY1,x,
KEY2,,x
KEY3,-,
```
````

The body must contain exactly one ```csv fence: a stem x choice matrix whose
header row lists every stem key (first cell is a throwaway label) and whose
rows name choice keys. Cell grammar, case-insensitive after trimming:

| Cell | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `x`  | correct for that stem |
| (empty) | eligible wrong answer |
| `-`  | never sampled into that stem (a per-stem exclusion, `min=0, max=0`) |

Notes:
- A pool choice with no matrix row is an eligible wrong answer everywhere.
- Every stem must appear in the header and must have at least one `x`.
- All key references are resolved at read time; a typo in a stem key, choice
  key, constraint member, or `apply_to` entry raises `ValueError` naming it.
- `questionsafe validate` checks metachoice files at the template level
  (no XML is rendered, since rendering requires generation parameters).

See `examples/markdown/metachoice.md` and `examples/metachoice_md.py` for a
worked example, and the MetaChoice page for the generation API.
